findings.title: order() maps flex order incorrectly to 2009 box ordinal-group
findings.body: The 2009 flexbox properties -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based (the default/initial value is 1, equivalent to flex order: 0), while the modern order property is 0-based. Passing $val unchanged means order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper and order(3) on .d-header .panel behave as order:1 and order:2 respectively in old WebKit/Firefox, and any future order(0) would be invalid/equal to the default. The mixin should emit $val + 1 for the box-ordinal-group properties to preserve the requested ordering across engines.

findings.title: Floated button inside new flex .small-action is no longer right-aligned
findings.body: .small-action is now display:flex (lines 263-265), so its direct children become flex items and float has no effect on flex items per the flexbox spec. The button rule at lines 306-310 still relies on float: right to push the action button to the far edge, which will now be ignored and the button will sit immediately after .small-action-desc in flow order. It needs margin-left: auto (or equivalent flex alignment) instead of/in addition to the dead float.

findings.title: align-items() emits an invalid -ms- property and omits the -moz- box equivalent
findings.body: Line 121 emits -ms-align-items, which is not a recognized IE10 property (the 2011 syntax is -ms-flex-align, already present on line 120), so it is dead CSS. Conversely the mixin emits the 2009 -webkit-box-align on line 118 and flexbox() claims -moz-box support, but there is no -moz-box-align, so old Firefox box-layout engines get no alignment while getting display:-moz-box from flexbox(). Add -moz-box-align and drop the invalid -ms-align-items.
